name: Lateral High-Plank Walk
definition: A dynamic bodyweight high-plank locomotion drill in which straight arms and wide-set feet maintain the prone bridge while the athlete shuffles sideways through the branded four-contact sequence, restores a stable high plank one position over, and trains both directions. The moving contacts are authored as support transitions rather than unsupported prime joint actions; the training-defining task is resisting spinal extension, rotation, and lateral flexion as the support base shifts. Abs and obliques are primary, and the upper- and lower-body support-chain roles are conservative anatomy-and-mechanics assignments. Upright lateral-band walks, forearm walking planks, bear crawls, push-ups, loaded drags, crossing steps, and forward or backward travel remain outside this contract.

variantAxes.description: The repetition begins on both palms and toes.
Both elbows remain extended during travel.
The feet begin slightly wider than hip width.
The lead leg moves first, followed by the opposite hand, then the lead hand and trailing leg.
Both lateral directions use mirrored contact sequences.
The trunk stays square against extension, rotation, and lateral flexion.
One four-contact shuffle that restores high plank counts once.
No guide constrains the lateral path.

execution.startingPosition: Set a high plank with straight arms, hands shoulder-width apart, and feet slightly wider than hip-width.
execution.movement: To travel left, step the left leg left, move the right hand left, then move the left hand and right leg left to restore the wide high plank.
execution.endpoint: Finish one position sideways with both palms and both feet grounded and the shoulders and hips still square.
execution.returnPhase: Repeat the mirrored four-contact sequence to the right when training the opposite direction.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep both elbows extended and resist low-back sag, trunk rotation, and side bending while contacts move.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the glutes engaged and maintain a straight line from shoulders through hips while the support base travels.
execution.sideOrDirection: Perform equal repetitions left and right; count each complete four-contact lateral step as one repetition.
disqualifyingCompensations: Crossing the hands or feet changes the reviewed shuffle sequence.
Dropping to the forearms changes the high-plank support fixture.
Travelling forward or backward changes the exercise direction.
